subject.title: [Bug]: Inbound pipeline misclassifies mention-only short messages as assistant reasoning

question: Should the owner pursue a narrowly traced core/history correction after obtaining a current Feishu-to-memory trace, or treat the reported `memory-tdai` record as an external-plugin integration boundary?
rationale: The issue combines a bundled Feishu normalization path with an external persistence surface and a provider-compatibility fallback; source evidence does not safely select a single owner or behavior change.

options.title: Trace before changing core
options.body: Obtain a sanitized current-version capture spanning Feishu parsing, history sanitization, and the memory writer, then implement only at the proven placeholder-entry boundary.

options.title: Route to external memory integration
options.body: If OpenClaw history never exposes the placeholder and only the external writer synthesizes or stores it, move the repair to that integration.

options.title: Preserve current core contract
options.body: If the current output is intentional provider-safe history representation and no channel-visible leak reproduces, document the boundary and close after a current reproduction check.

recommendation.title: Trace before changing core
recommendation.body: Obtain a sanitized current-version capture spanning Feishu parsing, history sanitization, and the memory writer, then implement only at the proven placeholder-entry boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The provider-turn-shape tradeoff is a cross-channel history contract, while Feishu ownership alone cannot decide it.
